title: Multipole Semantic Attention: A Fast Approximation of Softmax Attention for Pretraining
claim: Clustering queries and keys separately yields query-specific summaries that are selected semantically then spatially, before exact attention on a small subset.
layout: Single vertical panel: query bar top, two stacked cubes, key bar bottom, numbered steps 1-6
description: A tall single-panel diagram. A horizontal bar at the top shows queries split into segments A0, B0, A1, B1, A2, B2, with the first block greyed out and a blue marker on B2 labeled 'We follow this query for 4–6'. A matching bar at the bottom shows keys/values split into X0, Y0, X1, Y1, X2, Y2, with the last block greyed out. Between them are two isometric 2×2×3 cubes. The lower cube is green and tan and holds per-block summaries. Red arrows labeled 'Accumulate spatially' lead from it to the upper cube, which is blue and holds the accumulated summaries. A small axis legend marks key, query and block directions. Numbered colored labels and braces mark Steps 1–6: summarize, write specialized summaries, accumulate, semantic select, spatial select, attend exactly. The eye goes first to the cubes, then follows the steps.
caption: \ours{} method overview, depicting the far-field approximation. Bars: Queries (top) and keys/values (bottom) are partitioned by semantic cluster (A/B for queries, X/Y for keys) within each spatial block (0, 1, 2); segments vary in size because cluster membership is data-dependent. Lower cube: Per-block summaries indexed by (query cluster, key cluster, spatial block), constructed in Steps 1--2. Upper cube: Causally accumulated summaries (Step 3), accumulated along the spatial axis. Steps 4--6: A query in segment B2 (blue line) attends to the upper cube to select key cluster Y (Step 4, semantic selection), then to the lower cube to select spatial block 1 (Step 5, spatial selection), and finally attends exactly to keys in (Y, 1) (Step 6). Greyed-out segments do not participate: the first query block has no prior context, and the final key/value block is only accessed via local attention (computed separately). See Algorithm [ref] for pseudocode.
abstract: Pretraining transformers on long sequences (entire code repositories, collections of related documents) is bottlenecked by quadratic attention costs. We present Multipole Semantic Attention (MuSe), which accelerates 64k-context pretraining by 36% while matching baseline loss, requiring no architectural changes. MuSe clusters queries and keys separately in representation space. This yields query-specific summaries that substantially outperform spatial blocking at matched sparsity, while also enabling drop-in compatibility with existing pretrained models; we validate on Llama 3.1-8B and 3.2-1B without retraining. We pretrain language models up to 1B parameters at 64k context on code and scientific documents, confirming that MuSe preserves quality and long-context utilization during training.
